answer: In a haven restoring cedar buildings, agents could earn for verified pigment analyses rather than for opening accounts. Each customer funds a task with fresh sample data and a unique ID. Validators recompute the result, release escrow once, and mark that ID spent across all keys. A farm needs another completed task for each extra payout, costing computation and energy even in parallel. This assumes solvent escrow, reliable verification and no per-key subsidy; colluding customers cannot mint rewards, while newcomers can bid on small tasks.
